page_title: Every Product Needs a North Star Metric: Here’s How to Find Yours

summary.title: Every Product Needs a North Star Metric: Here's How to Find Yours
summary.one_liner: A North Star Metric is a single product metric that captures customer value and leads revenue; this Amplitude guide explains how to choose one using the "games" framework and input trees.
keywords: daily active users vs north star
how to pick a key metric for product team
takeaways: A good North Star Metric ties customer value to revenue, is a leading indicator, and reflects current product strategy.
Vanity metrics like daily active users or registered users are poor North Stars because they do not show customer value.
Companies should usually have one North Star per product, supported by 3-5 inputs that teams can influence.
Pick the core engagement 'game' your business plays (attention, transaction, or productivity) before choosing the metric.
Inputs are often framed by breadth, depth, frequency, and efficiency.
summary.summary: This Amplitude blog post introduces the North Star Framework, a product management model built on one metric that captures the customer value a product delivers. It explains the qualities of a good North Star (aligned to customer value, representing strategy, and a leading indicator) with examples such as mobile orders delivered and Facebook's early friend-adding metric. It covers why companies usually need only one North Star with 3-5 inputs, and how to pick one by identifying whether the business plays the attention, transaction, or productivity game. The post links to a longer North Star Playbook for deeper guidance.
